message.content: Selling both Park Place houses to cover the Tennessee rent. The dark-blue kill shot has to come down.
message.reasoning:
I need to decide how to liquidate assets to cover the $550 rent shortfall.

I sold two Boardwalk houses this turn for $100 each. I still need $349 to cover the $550 rent.

Monopoly building rules require selling houses evenly across properties. I can only sell houses from Park Place, which has two houses, because Boardwalk still has one.

Selling both Park Place houses would bring cash to $401, leaving a $149 shortfall. After that, I could sell the Boardwalk house for another $100 to reach $501. Once all buildings are removed, I could mortgage either Park Place or Boardwalk.

I will sell houses rather than declare bankruptcy. The remaining buildings are worth $300 in total, plus my current cash of $201, bringing the total to $501. That leaves a $49 shortfall, which I can cover by mortgaging either Park Place or Boardwalk.

Selling both Park Place houses now is the better choice. It minimizes decision rounds and leaves me with one house on Boardwalk, which is still legal under the even-building rule. I am also checking the rent table for Boardwalk to confirm the current rent amount.

Boardwalk rent drops to $100 with no buildings, and Park Place to $70. Neither is a kill shot. Declaring bankruptcy would let p1 inherit the dark blues with buildings intact and eliminate me. I must survive.

Boardwalk is the better property to keep unmortgaged. Its mortgage value of $200 exceeds Park Place's $175, and the 10% interest on unmortgage makes it more cost-effective. I am also checking whether a mortgaged property still receives doubled monopoly rent.

Mortgaged properties in a color group lose the monopoly rent bonus. The unmortgaged property receives only base rent, not doubled rent.

Mortgaging both dark blues would yield $375 total, but neither would collect rent. I need only $49 more to cover the shortfall.

Mortgaging Park Place for $175 is cheaper than mortgaging Boardwalk for $200. I will mortgage the cheaper property.

I will mortgage Park Place later rather than Boardwalk. Boardwalk is the stronger property to keep clear for rent. I am preparing a short public message and private notes. I am also checking the doubles situation.

I rolled doubles and landed on Tennessee. After paying the rent, I will roll again from that position. The orange properties are now worth $550 each with three houses, matching p1's holdings. I am also checking what happens on a roll of 2 from Tennessee.

Rolling a 3 from Tennessee lands on New York Avenue with three houses, costing $650. That is the most dangerous outcome. I cannot avoid this re-roll, so I will focus on surviving and sell two houses from Park Place.
